title: prefill-entropy-stabilizer-and-kernel-continuity-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: After integrating both FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels into the runtime, we have intermittent startup and small-batch tail-latency regressions for certain decoder-heavy workloads. These manifest as increased prefill time variance, kernel oscillation across requests, and elevated memory fragmentation on long-running hosts.

Goal: Design and implement an operational ‘Entropy Stabilizer’ layer plus a Kernel Continuity playbook that: 1) reduces prefill jitter for mixed workloads, 2) decreases kernel switching frequency during startup/hotpath, and 3) provides safe rollout/rollback controls tied to telemetry.

Scope: engineering work to instrument new signals, a lightweight runtime shim that applies per-request continuity decisions, an experiment harness for replaying traces against v2/v3 and hybrid modes, and an ops playbook for rollouts. This ticket focuses on the implementation, experiments, and a staged rollout for runtime-1.20.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th-percentile prefill latency on representative mixed-job suite improves or equals baseline by <=5% regression; 2) kernel_switch_count per request reduced by >40% during first 50 tokens for warm-cache cases; 3) no increase in OOM/restart events in canary cluster; 4) experiment reports and PRs merged; 5) Runbook added to console-ops doc.
work_items: implement Entropy Stabilizer shim that computes per-request continuity score and pins kernel for initial prefill window
build microbench harness to replay production traces deterministically against v2/v3/hybrid
add new config flags: continuity_window_tokens, continuity_confidence_threshold, entropy_decay_ms
run offline sweep across model profiles (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, long-context) and record decisions
add canary route and dashboard tiles for continuity metrics
doc playbook for rollout, canary thresholds, and rollback triggers
telemetry_queries: SELECT percentile_latency(0.95) FROM prefill_latencies WHERE model_family='decoder' AND route='canary-continuity'
SELECT count(*) FROM kernel_switch_events WHERE window_tokens<=50 GROUP BY host ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10
derive(memory_fragmentation) FROM allocator_heap_samples WHERE host IN (canary_hosts)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs behind feature flag; 2) Run offline replay across 24h trace corpus and validate against acceptance criteria; 3) Canary 5% traffic to continuity mode for low-risk customers for 48h; 4) Expand to 25% for 72h if no regressions; 5) Full rollout with monitoring automation and auto-fallback policy to legacy kernel selection on threshold breach.
rollback_plan: Immediate disable of continuity feature flag -> traffic falls back to existing kernel-selector. If metric drift is detected in canary (95th prefill latency +10% or >3 OOMs), trigger automated rollback and notify SREs. Keep diagnostic capture for 72h post-rollback.
notes: Prefill entropy score: lightweight heuristic combining request-length histogram, token-uniqueness estimate, and recent kernel_choice volatility.
Continuity window targets first 32-64 tokens by default; adjustable per-model via rollout config.
This approach prefers stability over marginal microbench throughput gains for first-chunk latency-sensitive workloads.
Related experimentation: try combining continuity pinning with microbatch shaping and allocator compaction triggers (follow-up ticket).
